name: SFML
workload: Megabunny: draw one million identical static bunny sprites per frame for 100 frames in a 1000x1000 window, reported as millions of bunnies per second (gettimeofday around the draw loop).
claimed_speedup: SFML 12.4 mbunnies/s versus raylib (C) 9.6 mbunnies/s, about 1.29x (derived from page data). The same table shows SDL2 with the OpenGL renderer at 21.9, so SFML is about 0.57x of SDL2 (derived from page data).
compiler_and_flags: From the benchmark's run.sh scripts: g++ -O3 for the SFML program, gcc -O3 for the raylib and SDL2 programs; SFML, raylib and SDL versions and their own build flags are not stated.
tradeoffs: Object-oriented C++ multimedia API (window, 2D graphics, audio, network) on top of OpenGL, with bindings for C, .NET, Ruby and Python. Per-sprite draw calls through sf::RenderWindow; the project is mid-move to version 3 and 2.x no longer gets features.
caveats: Third-party hobby benchmark ('My results' in the README) with no CPU or GPU model, no library versions and no vsync or driver information, so it is tier C, not A. The README itself says the benchmark is not a good reason to choose a framework. The workloads are not identical: the SDL2 program draws 32x32 destination rects with SDL_RenderCopy, SFML and raylib draw the texture at its own size, and the raylib loop also calls DrawFPS each frame; the timer includes first-frame costs. The table labels SFML as language 'C' although the source is main.cpp. SFML loses to SDL2 in the same table, so this is only a win over raylib. No SFML-owned benchmark exists in the SFML repo (README, no benchmark directory). An old first-party SFML forum benchmark (2007, topic 43 on en.sfml-dev.org, AMD Athlon 64 X2 3800+ and GeForce 7800 GT) reported 303 versus 9 frames on 2000 static sprites and 277 versus 3 on 2000 rotating sprites against SDL 1.2; that page is blocked here, so those numbers are WebSearch snippet only, and SDL 1.2 is obsolete (a search snippet also says SDL2 beats SFML in a later benchmark except dynamic text).
found_via: seed-record pass: README of https://github.com/SFML/SFML ('Simple and Fast Multimedia Library'); numbers found with WebSearch 'SFML vs SDL2 sprite rendering performance benchmark FPS' which led to https://github.com/electronstudio/megabunny
